correctness.rationale: The unsigned point-pair incidence matrix yields Laplacian eigenvalues n and 2(n−1) on the two mean-zero summands, giving the stated dipole potential. Fixing {1,2}→{1,3}, permutations of 4,…,n and reversal by (2 3) leave precisely two possible potential amplitudes. Both are generated by the dipole and its image under the symmetric intersection matrix; hence any equivariant map into the cut space is symmetric. This proves cut-projector uniqueness; taking the transpose of the difference of cycle projections proves the cycle version. Group averaging fixes each target pointwise, preserves the range condition, and contracts the operator norm for every p. The potential differences have multiplicities 1, 2(n−2), 2(n−3), n−3, 2(n−3)(n−2) respectively at 2α, α, α−β, 2β, β. Changing the cut diagonal to its complement gives the cycle column sum. Symmetry gives the row norms and the formulas give the claimed monotonicity, limits and n=5 values. Independent reduced-QR reconstruction at n=5,7,10 reproduced both absolute sums, including 2.1 and 2.5 at n=5. Replay: python3 branches/independent_checks.py 2 (NumPy).
residual_risks: The QR computation only corroborates canonical endpoint norms at three sizes, not unrestricted minimization. The proof is needed for the latter and for uniqueness only within the equivariant class.
